messages.subject: Regular (non-normalized) incomplete gamma function?
parts:
I have an unusual estimation problem that requires evaluating the expression:

log( lambda*( exp(-lambda*y) - lambda*y*Gamma(0,lambda*y) ) )

where Gamma(a,z) is the typical incomplete gamma function (from z to infinity).

The expression above is the solution to an integral that averages over uncertainty in a certain kind of censored exponential. The trouble is that Stan seems to have only normalized incomplete gamma functions. I've tried a few series approximations, but numerical issues are making it pretty unreliable.

Looks like what I need is tgamma(a,z) from Boost: http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_35_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/special/sf_gamma/igamma.html

Any ideas for how to approach this? Should I wait for tgamma(a,z) to get added in?

Btw, this is a small component of a larger hidden Markov model I've coded in Stan. The forward algorithm code in the manual helped me get that going right away. Thanks for the clear example. Every other piece of the model is working very smoothly.

messages.author: ca51dc784e0edba6
messages.subject: Re: Regular (non-normalized) incomplete gamma function?
parts:
One way is to ask the developers to include tgamma(a,z) into stan. this may take time, tho.

other way is to implement tgamma(a,z) into stan by yourself. See https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Contributing-New-Functions-to-Stan , https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Tutorial:-Using-a-User-Function-with-Gradients-in-CmdStan-v2.2.0-(aka-how-to-hack-around-Stan's-auto-diff) and source code, of course.
